Characterization Workflow

Suggested steps for characterizing a protein, checked off as you load the corresponding data.

Amino Acid (AA)
SS: Helix (H)ⓘ Secondary Structure (SS)
Combines predictions from: PSIPRED, SPIDER3, PSSPred4, DeepCNF-SS, NetSurfP-2.0.
Identifies alpha-helical, sheet, and pi-helical regions from sequence-based models.
SS: Pi-Helix (P)ⓘ Secondary Structure (SS)
Combines predictions from: PSIPRED, SPIDER3, PSSPred4, DeepCNF-SS, NetSurfP-2.0.
Identifies alpha-helical, sheet, and pi-helical regions from sequence-based models.
SS: Sheet (E)ⓘ Secondary Structure (SS)
Combines predictions from: PSIPRED, SPIDER3, PSSPred4, DeepCNF-SS, NetSurfP-2.0.
Identifies alpha-helical, sheet, and pi-helical regions from sequence-based models.
TM: Membrane (M)ⓘ Transmembrane Topology (TM)
Combines predictions from: TMHMM, Phobius, PolyPhobius.
Identifies membrane-spanning helical segments based on hydrophobicity and signal-peptide-aware HMMs.
DO: Disordered (D)ⓘ Disorder & Accessibility (DO)
Combines predictions from: NetSurfP-2.0, DISOPRED3, SPOT-Disorder, IUPred.
Flags intrinsically disordered, flexible, or non-crystallizable regions.
CC: Coiled Coils (C)ⓘ Coiled-Coil Domains (CC)
Combines predictions from: COILS, PCOILS, MARCOIL.
Flags heptad-repeat alpha-helical segments likely to form coiled coils.
Homologs: match qualityⓘ Homologs (HL) rows
One row per hit from HHpred, phmmer, BLAST or Foldseek. The glyph scale is shared - | strongest, then =, +, :, . weakest - but what it measures depends on the search:
HHpred: HHsearch match probability per column.
phmmer: HMMER posterior probability.
BLAST / Foldseek: BLOSUM62 substitution class (identical / positive / other).
Hover any cell for the exact basis, or the row's ℹ for the hit's E-value, identity and coverage.

ⓘ Ensemble variance (RMSF)
Per-residue fluctuation across the attached models, after superposing each model onto the first over the residues they share. High values mark the regions the models disagree about, so fold-level claims there are tentative.

Protein Summary ⓘ Protein Summary
Name, organism, EC, function text, keywords, GO terms and subcellular location, read from the fetched UniProt entry. Appears once a UniProt accession is loaded.
Scope: ⓘ Selection Scope
Full - click-and-drag selects a residue range across all rows.
Row - drags are locked to the row you start on, selecting horizontally along that row only.
Scale: ⓘ Horizontal Accordion Zoom
Residue columns stretch/shrink along the x-axis only; track heights stay locked so vertical alignment is always pixel-perfect.
Low zoom (under 12px/residue) hides residue letters and shows the tracks as continuous color blocks.
High zoom (12px/residue or more) fades the single-letter residue labels in, centered in each column.
Use − / +, or hold Ctrl while using the mouse wheel / middle button / trackpad pinch to zoom (anchored at your cursor). A plain wheel scroll just scrolls vertically.

Protein constants ⓘ Protein constants
Computed offline from the loaded sequence using standard average monomer masses to ensure consistency across the session: molecular weight, isoelectric point (pI), net charge at pH 7, molar extinction coefficient, and hydropathy index (e.g., GRAVY).

Caveats. Charge and pI calculations assume standard unmodified termini and functional groups. Extinction calculations account only for canonical monomers; mature fluorophores, chromophores, or secondary chemical modifications that dominate absorbance are not included and require empirical or literature values.

Usage. Useful for construct design in that extreme pI values or high hydropathy predict poor solubility, aggregation, or non-ideal behavior during purification and ion exchange.
No sequence loaded.
Quantitative Metrics
ⓘ Quantitative Metrics
Structural statistics computed from attached PDB / CIF / AlphaFold JSON files for the current selection.

pLDDT - AlphaFold's per-residue confidence score (1-100). Hover the pLDDT row's ⓘ for full score bands.
RSA - Relative Solvent Accessibility (0.0-1.0). Hover the RSA row's ⓘ for full score bands.

Requires at least one structure file attached above.

Cross-reference dropdown - pick any loaded SS/TM/DO/CC track or pLDDT/RSA model to see how the current selection (manual range, or a row/band/residue-type filter) overlaps with it, shown below the metrics above.

For pLDDT/RSA, All/Apo/Holo/oligomeric-state (Monomer/Dimer/Trimer/...) mass-selections are also available - each shows every matching model's stats individually, plus an Average of N summary line when more than one model is included.
Select a region or graph point for statistics.
Track Visibility (full manager)

Every track, grouped by type, with its own show/hide. View as, Color, Filter and per-type Config live in the quick controls popover.

Rules (contradiction / co-localization)

Flag residues satisfying a boolean query across tracks (e.g. disorder ∧ TM ∧ low pLDDT). Each enabled rule becomes a coloured track; "select" turns its matches into a selection.

Presets (curated rules)

Literature-backed rules, suggested from your guide answers and loaded data. Add one and tweak it in the editor.

Interfaces (oligomer contacts)

Find residues at chain–chain interfaces in the active (or first) multi-chain structure. Runs client-side, so it works on AlphaFold / ESMFold models too; each chain gets an interface track.

Ensemble variance (RMSF)

Per-residue fluctuation across the attached models, in angstroms, after superposing each model onto the first over the residues they share. Needs at least two models of the same construct; residues are matched by their own numbering. The result is an Ensemble variance row (blue = rigid, red = mobile).

Cross-checks (independent predictions)

Compares two independent reads of the same question. TM consensus vs Quick2D TM flags every residue where the pasted topology consensus and the Quick2D transmembrane call disagree, so inspect those before trusting either. Runs client-side.

Evaluation Guide

The Protein Guide is an interactive characterization workflow that recommends and tracks steps based on the protein's profile.

ChimeraX Command:ⓘ Visualization Command
A ready-to-paste command (select / color / label) built from the current selection and target above, in whichever tool's syntax is chosen in Options > Command Engine (ChimeraX by default).

-
Change engine (ChimeraX / PyMOL / VMD) in Options.
Construct designer (truncated FASTA)

Turns the annotations into a wet-lab construct: strip the disordered termini, or keep the current selection, then export the construct as FASTA. Only a terminal disordered stretch of at least N residues is trimmed, so a short tail or a single stray residue is left alone. Primer design is out of scope.

Options

Command Engine

Which tool's syntax the sidebar's Target/Command panel generates.

Annotation Colors

Choose a colour set for the annotation types (H/P/E/C/M/D) used in the heatmap cells, row badges, and legend. The colourblind-safe option follows the Okabe-Ito palette; high-contrast picks stronger tints for low-vision users.

Review aids

Aids for reviewing the app itself. External services (network calls) live under Storage.

Conservation Scoring

How the CONSERVATION row is computed (1 = fully conserved, 0 = fully divergent) from the variant FASTA sequences uploaded via Attach, and how those sequences are aligned onto the reference AA sequence. Changes apply to the heatmap row immediately and are saved with the session.

Feeds

The CONSERVATION row drives the Rules engine and the 3D conservation colouring.

Membrane topology

Paste the output of a topology predictor to add it as a per-residue inside / TM-helix / outside track: TMHMM/Phobius segments (inside 1 11, TMhelix 12 30), a DeepTMHMM JSON, or a TOPCONS-style per-residue line (TOPCONS ooooMMMMiiii). Add two or more sources to also get a majority-vote Consensus track; columns where they disagree are marked ? rather than guessed.

Run in-app
Source
Open DeepTMHMM ↗

Domain families

Scan the loaded sequence for domain families. hmmscan searches Pfam; InterProScan runs several member databases at once, including NCBIfam for bacterial and viral families.

Source
Open InterProScan ↗

Homolog search

Search Swiss-Prot in-app and add one Homologs row per significant hit (they feed conservation, the match-quality colouring and the template table). For a curated MSA, run HHpred externally and attach the resulting .hhr in Input Data.

Source
Open HHpred ↗

Structure models & validation

AlphaFold is fetched automatically with a UniProt accession (Input Data -> Find UniProt accession, or the guide's structure step). ESMFold folds the sequence directly (max 400 aa). Validation reads the wwPDB quality data for an attached experimental entry.

Sources
Open AlphaFold DB ↗ Open RCSB PDB ↗

Experimental per-residue data

The lab-measured layer: DMS mutation tolerance, HDX protection, NMR order parameters, per-residue simulation output or any per-residue score. Paste position value lines (space, tab, comma, colon or semicolon), one series of at least five values, or a named table with a header row such as resid,rmsf,rmsd,sasa - every numeric column then becomes its own row, which is how a trajectory analysis drops in. The row plots like the ensemble-variance row (switch it to a graph in Track Control's View as) and is cross-read against conservation.

values map 1:1 onto the reference sequence
Formats

One position value per line, a bare series of ≥5 values, or a named table with a header row (each numeric column becomes its own row).

Stability predictions (dG)

There is no stable API for ddG (folding-stability change on mutation), so this is a hand-off: copy the mutation list (or the sequence) into one of the linked services, run it, then paste its result back. Lines like R175H -1.2 (negative = destabilising) become an experimental row, so it overlays with conservation, the structure and the 3D colour picker like any other evidence.

Run on a service
Open DynaMut2 ↗ Open DUET ↗ Open mCSM ↗ Open FoldX suite ↗

Structural homology (Foldseek)

Search a structure database for structural relatives of the active (or first attached) model. Needs at least one attached structure.

Source
Open Foldseek ↗

Variant effects

Assess every loaded variant substitution with all applicable sources: AlphaMissense (human, needs a UniProt accession), Ensembl VEP/SIFT (species-specific, needs a species), conservation, structure context and curated UniProt features. Attach a variant FASTA first.

AlphaMissense coverage ↗

Ensembl VEP runs in-app above. These take the same substitutions but have no usable API: copy the list and paste it in.

External services

API access is on by default on the deployed site (and off on a local file:// page); turn it off or on here. The activity log records every request and what came back - open it from the menu bar ("Log") or here.

Privacy

Only the requested term, sequence or accession is sent to a public service; nothing is uploaded otherwise.

Save File

Export the full current session - sequence, attached structures, selection, and preferences - as a portable .json file you can move to another browser or machine. To bring one back in, attach it via the toolbar's Attach Structure(s) or JSON button like any other file - Q2DV recognizes it automatically from a marker inside the file, without needing a separate import control.

This is a different, restorable format from the Data modal's "Raw JSON" export, which is a read-only report and can't be re-imported.

The save stays small because it never embeds the raw PDB/CIF text - it only references locally-attached files by hash. On the machine that created it, 3D models come right back from that device's structure cache; on another machine, Data > Structure Files lists which files need re-attaching (or use Find to locate them in a folder).

Cached Data

Your pasted Quick2D text, the pLDDT/RSA data derived from attached structure files, current selection, and view preferences are saved automatically in this browser (via localStorage) so they survive a page refresh or reopening this tab later. Nothing is uploaded anywhere - it never leaves your device.

Note: this session cache does NOT include the raw structure file text - that lives in the separate, device-local structure cache below, so clearing the input data won't delete your cached PDB/CIF copies.

No cached data yet.
Clear input data removes the sequence, structures, annotations and selection but keeps your preferences. Clear all data also wipes preferences and the welcome state. Cached PDB/CIF copies below are left intact by both.

Local Structure Cache (this device)

Raw PDB/CIF text you've attached is cached on this device (via IndexedDB) so 3D models reappear instantly after a refresh or a save re-import - never re-uploading the same file twice. It never leaves this device and is not embedded in exported saves, so a save taken to another machine will ask for its local files there (Data > Structure Files > Find to locate them). Old copies no longer referenced by the current session are automatically evicted, oldest-first, beyond the 100 MB soft cap.

Clearing this is separate from the cache controls above - use it only when you want to free up space without touching the data you have loaded.

Homolog Templates

Every Homologs row - imported from an .hhr, searched in-app (phmmer/BLAST) or found with Foldseek - ranked by a template score (confidence × identity × query coverage, 0-100). Confidence is the source's probability where it has one (HHpred, Foldseek); for phmmer and BLAST it comes from the E-value (10 points per decade). Structure shows a cached file, an auto-fetchable PDB entry, or the AlphaFold model for the hit's accession.

Structure Files

Each PDB/CIF file is scanned on upload for a rough protein classification, apo/holo ligand state, and oligomeric state (chain count). This is best-effort: many files - especially computational models like AlphaFold predictions - simply don't record this information, in which case it's reported as such rather than guessed.

No structure files attached yet.

Co-localization

One row per residue with the metrics that apply to it side by side: conservation, pLDDT, RSA, ensemble RMSF, the annotation types present, and how close it sits to each cofactor. Rows come from the current selection or from a rule's matches, so a boolean query can be read against the numbers behind it.

Raw JSON

The same data above, in one ordered columns/rows structure - safe to expand with more columns later, or pull into another tool.
This is a read-only report - attaching it back into Q2DV won't restore a session. For that, use Options > Export Save.

Welcome to Quick2DViewer

This is a tool for viewing protein sequence information, structure annotations, and other information together in a unified view. If this is your first time using Q2DV, it's recommended to click Show me around for a quick tour of the interface and how to get started.

You can access this tutorial from Help → Getting started.

Help

New here? Open Getting started for the welcome panel and a short tour. Every ⓘ icon throughout the page (legend, row labels, sidebar fields) explains that specific piece in place.

Quick start

  1. Load a protein - Input Data: pick an example protein, paste Quick2D output, or attach a PDB/CIF/JSON/save file.
  2. Fetch data - File ▸ Data Sources… opens every source in one window (UniProt, topology, domains, homologs, structure, variants, and more).
  3. Explore - the sidebar tabs: Selection, Tracks, Analyze, Guide and Commands.
  4. Export - the Export menu: session save, figures, TSV/CSV, structure file, methods summary and 3D commands.
  5. Find things - the Jump to… box in the header, and the ⓘ icons throughout.

Activity log

The last 200 actions this session, newest first: clicks, menu choices, API jobs (submit, poll, result, what was parsed) and task starts/finishes. Session-only, nothing is sent anywhere. Useful for debugging a run that produced nothing, and for reconstructing a workflow; q2dvActions() in the console returns the same log as JSON (a starting point for macros). 

(no actions recorded yet this session)

Macros

Macros are pre-recorded action sequences. Q2DV allows for saving or running macros to sequentially run actions across different proteins. This can automate API calls and import steps of a workflow and replay them, enabling analysis to be repeated or moved to another protein. Each step stores the action, its resolved provider and its parameters; $ACCESSION stands for the session accession, so the override below retargets the whole run. Replay calls the same code paths as the buttons, and every step lands in the activity log.

Hypothesis read-out

Ranks positions by combined evidence (conservation, burial, model confidence, curated sites, homolog coverage) and suggests a test for each. These are suggestions to evaluate, not conclusions: every row carries the evidence that drove it, low-confidence regions are excluded, and known variants are marked so you compare before designing new ones. For a structureless membrane protein this is the characterisation shortlist to take into simulations or assays.
